ConnectionStrings.// Rekfar: Empty on purpose — the API refuses to start without it. Locally: dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Rekfar" "Server=localhost,1433;Database=Rekfar;..." --project src/Rekfar.Api. In Azure the logical server is Entra-only, so there is no password to store: Server=tcp:rekfar.database.windows.net,1433;Database=Rekfar;Authentication=Active Directory Default;Encrypt=True;

Database.// CommandTimeoutSeconds: Above the 30s ADO.NET default. The free-offer database is serverless and auto-pauses, so the first query after an idle period waits on a resume that can take tens of seconds.

Cors.// AllowedOrigins: Deliberately empty: the API refuses to start without an explicit origin, and every environment names its own. Note that configuration merges arrays by index, so a non-empty default here would leak entries into environments that override only the first.

Hosting.// TrustForwardedHeaders: True only where an ingress overwrites X-Forwarded-For. Trusting it anywhere else lets a caller forge the address the rate limiter partitions on.

RateLimiting.//: Per caller, per window, on /v1 only. A map client refetches on every pan and zoom, so this has to clear normal browsing comfortably — it is here to stop abuse, not to shape traffic.
